A_target.statement:
Let $F: \mathbf C \to \mathbf D$ be [[Definition:Left Adjoint|left adjoint]] to $G$.
Then $F$ preserves all [[Definition:Colimit|colimits]] which exist in $\mathbf C$.

B_source.statement: A [[Definition:Right Adjoint|right adjoint]] preserves all limits which exist in its domain.

object_map.reformulation: Pass to opposite categories, where the left adjoint becomes a right adjoint and colimits become limits.

validity_conditions: Reversing arrows turns the hom-set bijection of F -| G into one exhibiting G^op -| F^op.
For example, the free group functor sends disjoint unions to free products, and tensoring with a module is right exact.
proof_plan: The bijection $\map {\operatorname {Hom}_{\mathbf D} } {F X, Y} \cong \map {\operatorname {Hom}_{\mathbf C} } {X, G Y}$ reads in the opposite categories as $\map {\operatorname {Hom}_{\mathbf D^{\text {op} } } } {Y, F X} \cong \map {\operatorname {Hom}_{\mathbf C^{\text {op} } } } {G Y, X}$.
Hence $G^{\text {op} } \dashv F^{\text {op} }$, so $F^{\text {op} }$ is a right adjoint.
A colimit in $\mathbf C$ is a limit in $\mathbf C^{\text {op} }$, which $F^{\text {op} }$ preserves by the source result.
